title: The Uniform Distribution
quickIdea: Spread probability evenly over an interval: the density is the constant 1/(b-a), so the probability of a subinterval is just its length over the total length.
remember: Density f(x) = 1/(b - a) for a <= x <= b and 0 elsewhere; CDF F(x) = (x - a)/(b - a) inside the interval.
Mean (a + b)/2, variance (b - a)^2/12, standard deviation (b - a)/(2 sqrt 3), which is about 0.289(b - a) - noticeably less than half the range.
P(c <= X <= d) = (d - c)/(b - a): a ratio of lengths, no integration needed once the density is constant.
The density can exceed 1: on (0, 0.5) it is 2. Only the area is a probability.
The discrete uniform on {1, ..., N} is a different distribution: mean (N + 1)/2 and variance (N^2 - 1)/12. Do not mix the two formulas; GATE has used the continuous one on a continuous interval.

Open endpoints do not matter for a continuous variable, so (1, 6) and [1, 6] give identical probabilities - which is why the 2019 question can say 'open interval' and still count the endpoint 2 as favourable.

example.prompt: Y is uniform on (1, 6). The polynomial 3x^2 + 6xY + 3Y + 6 in x has only real roots for which Y, and with what probability?
example.work: A quadratic ax^2 + bx + c has only real roots when b^2 - 4ac >= 0. Here a = 3, b = 6Y and c = 3Y + 6, so the condition is 36Y^2 - 12(3Y + 6) >= 0, that is 36(Y^2 - Y - 2) >= 0, that is (Y - 2)(Y + 1) >= 0. So Y <= -1 or Y >= 2. Inside (1, 6) only Y >= 2 survives, which is the subinterval [2, 6) of length 4 out of a total length 5.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2019 Q.47 combines the uniform distribution with a discriminant condition, and it is a two-step question: solve the inequality first, then measure the favourable set. The distribution never enters the inequality, so a candidate who tries to integrate the density before solving the condition wastes the marks' time budget.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2019 Q.47: Y is uniform on the open interval (1, 6). The probability that 3x^2 + 6xY + 3Y + 6 has only real roots is ______ (one decimal place).
variations.why: The discriminant condition reduces to (Y - 2)(Y + 1) >= 0, so the favourable set inside (1, 6) is [2, 6), of length 4. Dividing by the total length 5 gives 0.8. Note that Y = 2 is included because a double root is still a real root, and the density is 1/5 there.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: X is uniform on (0, 10). Find P(2 < X < 7), the mean and the standard deviation.
variations.why: The interval has length 5 out of 10. The mean is the midpoint and the standard deviation is (b - a)/(2 sqrt 3) = 10/3.4641 = 2.8868, well under half the range.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: X is uniform on (0, 1). For which a is P(X > a) = 0.25, and what is the probability that X^2 < 0.25?
variations.why: The first is a length condition: 1 - a = 0.25. The second needs the event rewritten as X < 0.5 before the uniform length is read, and it is the same move the GATE DA CDF question makes with X^2 <= 0.25.

trap.what: Using the discrete-uniform formulas on a continuous interval, or forgetting that the favourable set must be intersected with the support.
trap.why: The two uniforms have different means and variances, and a condition such as Y <= -1 can be satisfied by the inequality while being outside the interval the variable lives on.
trap.counterexample: For the 2019 question, the inequality also holds for Y <= -1, but no probability sits there because Y lives on (1, 6). Counting the whole real line would give a 'probability' larger than 1. And for N = 6 the discrete formula gives variance 35/12 = 2.917, whereas the continuous uniform on (1, 6) has variance 25/12 = 2.083.

check.question: X is uniform on (2, 8). Find P(X < 5) and the standard deviation.
check.explanation: The subinterval (2, 5) has length 3 out of 6, so the probability is 1/2 - which is also clear because 5 is the midpoint. The standard deviation is (8 - 2)/(2 sqrt 3) = 6/3.4641 = 1.7321.
